questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision in which she was an unrestrained driver. She is alert and hemodynamically stable but reports right flank pain. Examination reveals right upper quadrant and right flank tenderness without rebound. Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrates kidneys of normal size and contour, with the right kidney positioned approximately 1.5 cm inferior to the left—reported as a normal anatomic variant. Both adrenal glands appear unremarkable. Which of the following most directly accounts for the inferior position of the right kidney compared with the left?
choices: Liver in the right upper quadrant
explanations: Incorrect. Adrenal glands sit superior to both kidneys but do not normally displace either kidney inferiorly.
Incorrect. The diaphragm overlaps the upper third of both kidneys symmetrically and does not produce side-to-side asymmetry.
Correct. The right lobe of the liver occupies space superior to the right kidney, displacing it inferiorly relative to the left.
Incorrect. The psoas major lies posterior to both kidneys without producing positional asymmetry.
Incorrect. The right renal artery is in fact longer than the left because the aorta lies left of midline.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with a 3-cm renal mass on the lower pole of the right kidney is undergoing open partial nephrectomy through a posterior flank incision. After dividing the latissimus dorsi and reflecting the 12th rib superiorly, the surgeon enters the retroperitoneum and identifies the posterior surface of the lower pole of the right kidney. Immediately deep to the kidney along its lateral aspect lies a flat, broad muscle that runs vertically from the iliac crest to the 12th rib. Which of the following muscles is the surgeon most likely identifying?
explanations: Incorrect. The external oblique is part of the anterior abdominal wall and is not posterior to the kidney.
Incorrect. The iliacus lies in the iliac fossa and is not a posterior relation of the kidney.
Incorrect. The latissimus dorsi is superficial and has already been divided in this approach.
Incorrect. The medial aspect of the psoas major lies posterior to the kidney; the lateral aspect does not.
Correct. The lateral aspect of the quadratus lumborum lies immediately posterior to the lower pole of the kidney.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man with a body mass index of 17.5 kg/m² is brought to the emergency department after a fall onto his left side from a ladder. He is hemodynamically stable but reports severe left flank pain and gross hematuria. Examination shows left costovertebral angle tenderness. CT demonstrates a Grade III renal laceration of the left kidney with a perinephric hematoma. The trauma surgeon notes that patients with low body fat are at increased risk of blunt renal injury because of attenuation of the structure that normally cushions the kidney from external force. Which of the following best describes the primary function of that structure?
explanations: Incorrect. Urine concentration occurs in the renal pyramids of the medulla, not in perinephric fat.
Correct. Perinephric (perirenal) fat surrounds the kidney and provides cushioning and support, especially given that the kidneys receive minimal protection from the ribs.
Incorrect. Glomerular filtration is a function of the renal corpuscle in the cortex.
Incorrect. Mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone are produced by the adrenal cortex.
Incorrect. Voluntary urinary continence is provided by the external urethral sphincter, not perinephric fat.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension undergoes a renal biopsy as part of evaluation for proteinuria. On low-power microscopy the pathologist identifies the cone-shaped striated structures of the renal medulla, which contain longitudinally oriented tubules including the loops of Henle and the collecting ducts. These structures are most directly responsible for which of the following physiologic processes?
explanations: Incorrect. Erythropoietin is produced by interstitial cells of the cortex, not within the medullary pyramids.
Incorrect. Glomerular filtration occurs in the renal corpuscle of the cortex.
Incorrect. Glucose reabsorption occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule of the cortex.
Incorrect. Renin is released from juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole in the cortex.
Correct. The renal pyramids contain the loops of Henle and collecting ducts, which together generate concentrated urine.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man passes a 4-mm calcium oxalate stone after several hours of severe right flank pain that radiated to the groin. CT obtained before passage demonstrated the stone within the renal pelvis, just proximal to its junction with the ureter. The stone formed within a renal papilla and traveled through the upper urinary tract before lodging at this location. Through which of the following structures did urine most recently pass before reaching the renal pelvis?
explanations: Correct. The drainage path is renal papilla → minor calyx → major calyx → renal pelvis → ureter, so urine most recently passed through a major calyx before reaching the renal pelvis.
Incorrect. Minor calyces empty into major calyces, which then drain into the renal pelvis.
Incorrect. The renal capsule is fibrous connective tissue surrounding the kidney and does not transmit urine.
Incorrect. Renal columns are extensions of cortical tissue between pyramids and carry vessels, not urine.
Incorrect. The renal cortex is the site of filtration and early modification but does not feed directly into the renal pelvis.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old man comes to the emergency department with the abrupt onset of severe right-sided colicky flank pain that radiates to his right testicle. He is afebrile and unable to find a comfortable position. Vital signs are stable. Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows a 6-mm radiopaque calculus impacted along the course of the right ureter. At which of the following anatomic sites is impaction most likely?
choices: Distal to the renal hilum within the renal pelvis
Pelvic ureter posterior to the rectum
Where the ureter crosses the common iliac vessels
Where the ureter is crossed by the gonadal artery
explanations: Incorrect. The renal pelvis itself is not one of the three classic narrowings; the proximal narrowing is the ureteropelvic junction.
Incorrect. The mid-ureter overlies the psoas without anatomic narrowing.
Incorrect. The ureter does not pass posterior to the rectum.
Correct. The three classic ureteral narrowings are the ureteropelvic junction, the pelvic brim where the ureter crosses the common iliac vessels, and the ureterovesical junction.
Incorrect. Crossing by the gonadal artery is not a recognized site of stone impaction.

questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman with menorrhagia from symptomatic uterine fibroids undergoes total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. On postoperative day 2 she develops left flank pain. CT urography demonstrates left hydronephrosis with abrupt cutoff of contrast at the level of the cardinal ligament near the cervical stump. The injury most likely occurred where the pelvic ureter normally passes:
choices: Anterior to the common iliac artery
explanations: Incorrect. The ureter crosses anterior to the common iliac vessels at the pelvic brim, well above the cervix.
Incorrect. The ureter passes inferior—not anterior—to the uterine artery.
Incorrect. The ovarian artery does not have a defining surgical relationship with the ureter at the cervix.
Correct. The pelvic ureter passes inferior to the uterine artery ("water under the bridge"), making it vulnerable to injury during hysterectomy near the cardinal ligament.
Incorrect. The ureter enters the posterior bladder wall obliquely; injury near the cervix is mediated through its relation with the uterine artery.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old girl is referred for evaluation of recurrent febrile urinary tract infections. She has had three episodes of pyelonephritis in the past 18 months despite appropriate antibiotic treatment. Renal ultrasound demonstrates mild bilateral hydronephrosis. A voiding cystourethrogram shows retrograde flow of contrast from the bladder into both ureters during voiding, reaching the renal pelvis on the right. The anatomic feature that normally prevents this finding depends on which of the following?
choices: Active dilation of the ureteric orifices
Mucosal valve at the ureteropelvic junction
Oblique passage through the bladder wall
Peristaltic activity of ureteral smooth muscle
explanations: Incorrect. Ureteric orifices are passively compressed during voiding, not actively dilated.
Incorrect. The external urethral sphincter governs urinary continence but does not affect vesicoureteral reflux.
Incorrect. There is no discrete valve at the ureteropelvic junction.
Correct. The ureters pass obliquely through the bladder wall; bladder contraction compresses the intramural segment and prevents reflux. Failure of this mechanism produces vesicoureteral reflux.
Incorrect. Peristalsis propels urine antegrade but does not by itself prevent retrograde flow at the bladder wall.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with painless gross hematuria undergoes diagnostic cystoscopy. The urologist describes a smooth, triangular region on the posterior internal bladder wall, the boundaries of which are defined by three openings. A papillary urothelial lesion is identified within this region. The three corners of this triangular area are formed by which of the following structures?
choices: Apex, body, and neck of the bladder
Internal and external urethral orifices and the apex
Median umbilical ligament and the two ureteric orifices
Two ureteric orifices and the apex of the bladder
Two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice
explanations: Incorrect. Apex, body, and neck describe regions of the bladder, not corners of the trigone.
Incorrect. The external urethral orifice is at the distal end of the urethra, not within the bladder.
Incorrect. The median umbilical ligament marks the apex externally and is not a corner of the trigone.
Incorrect. The trigone does not include the apex.
Correct. The trigone is bounded by the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice on the posterior internal bladder wall.

questions.stem: A 76-year-old woman reports urinary urgency and several episodes of urge incontinence per week. Urodynamic testing during the storage phase reveals involuntary contractions of the muscle that empties the bladder, with detrusor pressures exceeding 50 cm H2O. The muscle responsible for these contractions has which of the following characteristics?
choices: Smooth muscle that contracts during filling
Smooth muscle that contracts during voiding
Striated muscle of the pelvic floor
Visceral muscle confined to the trigone
explanations: Incorrect. The detrusor is smooth, not skeletal, muscle and is not under direct voluntary control.
Incorrect. The detrusor relaxes during filling; contraction during filling is the abnormality, not normal physiology.
Correct. The detrusor is smooth muscle that relaxes during bladder filling and contracts during micturition.
Incorrect. The pelvic floor (levator ani) is striated muscle but does not empty the bladder.
Incorrect. The detrusor surrounds the entire bladder, not just the trigone.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old previously healthy woman presents with her fourth urinary tract infection in the past 12 months. She reports dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic discomfort that began 2 days ago. She is sexually active with a single male partner. Pelvic and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria. She asks why she is so prone to recurrent infection compared with her brother. Which of the following anatomic features is the principal explanation for the increased susceptibility of women to UTI?
choices: Lack of an internal urethral sphincter
explanations: Incorrect. Urine glucose does not differ in a sex-dependent manner that explains UTI risk.
Incorrect. Both sexes possess an internal urethral sphincter at the bladder neck.
Incorrect. Urinary pH is not the anatomic basis for the female predisposition to UTI.
Correct. The female urethra is short (about 4 cm) and lies close to the rectum, allowing bacteria to ascend more readily into the bladder.
Incorrect. Bladder neck caliber is not the principal explanation for the female predisposition to UTI.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man comes to his primary care physician because of a 6-month history of progressive urinary hesitancy, weak stream, and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying. He reports waking 3 times per night to urinate. He denies dysuria, hematuria, or fever. Vital signs are within normal limits. Digital rectal examination reveals a symmetrically enlarged, smooth, non-tender prostate without nodules.
explanations: Incorrect. Although the bladder neck is adjacent, BPH-related obstruction is mediated through compression of the urethral segment passing through the prostate.
Incorrect. The external urethral sphincter is distal to the prostate and is not compressed by prostatic enlargement.
Incorrect. The membranous urethra passes through the perineal membrane, distal to the prostate.
Correct. The prostatic urethra passes through the prostate; benign prostatic hyperplasia compresses this segment, producing hesitancy and incomplete emptying.
Incorrect. The spongy urethra runs through the penis, well distal to the prostate.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with paraplegia is brought to the emergency department after attempted urethral catheterization in a long-term care facility was met with strong resistance. The staff reportedly applied additional force, after which the patient developed perineal pain and was unable to urinate. Examination reveals scrotal swelling and bruising of the perineum without evidence of penile injury. Retrograde urethrogram demonstrates contrast extravasation into the space deep to the perineal membrane. Rupture of which segment of the urethra is most likely responsible?
explanations: Incorrect. The bladder neck is proximal to the perineal membrane; injury here would not extravasate deep to it.
Incorrect. The external urethral orifice is the distal opening on the glans and is not the site of perineal extravasation.

Correct. The membranous urethra passes through the perineal membrane and is relatively fixed and narrow, so forceful catheterization can rupture it, with extravasation into the space deep to the perineal membrane.
Incorrect. The prostatic urethra is proximal to the perineal membrane.
Incorrect. Spongy urethral injury produces extravasation along the penis and scrotum, not deep to the perineal membrane.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is undergoing pelvic floor physical therapy after a pelvic fracture. His therapist asks him to start and stop his urinary stream voluntarily. The therapist explains that the muscle being recruited is composed of skeletal muscle innervated by a somatic nerve. Which of the following best describes this muscle?
choices: Levator ani at the bladder neck
explanations: Incorrect. The detrusor is smooth muscle under autonomic control.
Correct. The external urethral sphincter is composed of skeletal muscle and is innervated by the pudendal nerve, allowing voluntary control of urination.
Incorrect. The internal urethral sphincter is smooth muscle under autonomic (involuntary) control.
Incorrect. The levator ani provides pelvic floor support but is not the urethral sphincter.
Incorrect. The trigone is a sensory region; it does not provide voluntary motor control of the urinary stream.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman is found to have a 5-cm right renal cell carcinoma on imaging performed for back pain. CT angiography demonstrates a tumor thrombus extending into the renal artery. Preoperative planning requires identification of the artery's origin. The right renal artery is a direct branch of which of the following vessels?
explanations: Correct. Both renal arteries arise directly from the abdominal aorta, just below the level of the superior mesenteric artery.
Incorrect. The celiac trunk supplies foregut structures, not the kidney.
Incorrect. The common iliac arteries supply the pelvic and lower-limb circulations.
Incorrect. The inferior mesenteric artery supplies hindgut structures.
Incorrect. The superior mesenteric artery supplies the midgut; the renal artery does not arise from it.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is undergoing CT angiography of the abdomen for evaluation of an incidental finding. The radiologist measures the left renal vein at 7 cm and the right renal vein at 2.5 cm. Which of the following anatomic relationships best explains this length disparity?
choices: Left renal vein crosses anterior to the aorta
Left renal vein passes posterior to the aorta
Left renal vein receives the left adrenal vein
Right kidney is positioned inferior to the left
Right renal artery is shorter than the left
explanations: Correct. The IVC lies to the right of the aorta, so the left renal vein must cross anterior to the aorta (passing under the SMA) to reach it, accounting for its greater length.
Incorrect. In standard anatomy the left renal vein passes anterior, not posterior, to the aorta.
Incorrect. The left renal vein does receive the adrenal vein, but this is not the basis for its greater length.
Incorrect. Vertical kidney position does not determine renal vein length.
Incorrect. The right renal artery is in fact longer than the left because the aorta lies left of midline.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with a 4-month history of intermittent left flank pain and gross hematuria. He has also noted a new "bag of worms" sensation in the left scrotum. He has no significant past medical history. Vital signs are normal. Examination confirms a left-sided varicocele that decreases when supine. CT angiography shows compression of the left renal vein in the angle between two abdominal vessels, with proximal venous dilation.
questions.diagram: Left renal vein in the SMA-aorta angle
choices: Celiac trunk and left diaphragmatic crus
explanations: Incorrect. The IVC does not compress the left renal vein.
Incorrect. The celiac trunk arises well above the renal veins.
Incorrect. The inferior mesenteric artery arises below the renal veins and is not the artery in nutcracker syndrome.
Incorrect. The right renal artery and liver are not in the path of the left renal vein.
Correct. Nutcracker syndrome results from compression of the left renal vein between the SMA and the aorta, producing flank pain, hematuria, and a left-sided varicocele.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man with primary infertility is found on physical examination to have a left-sided varicocele. The right hemiscrotum is normal. Doppler ultrasound confirms reflux in the left pampiniform plexus. Which of the following anatomic facts best explains the side-specific occurrence of varicocele in this patient?
choices: Left gonadal vein drains directly into the IVC
Left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein
Right gonadal vein drains into the inferior mesenteric vein
Right gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein
Right gonadal vein drains into the portal vein
explanations: Incorrect. It is the right gonadal vein that drains directly into the IVC.
Correct. The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein, which is at higher pressure and can be externally compressed; this predisposes to a left-sided varicocele.
Incorrect. The right gonadal vein drains into the IVC, not the IMV (a portal tributary).
Incorrect. The right gonadal vein drains into the IVC, not the left renal vein.
Incorrect. Gonadal venous drainage is systemic, not portal.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old multiparous woman reports a 2-year history of dull, chronic pelvic pain that worsens with prolonged standing and just before menses. She has had three pregnancies, each complicated by venous insufficiency in the third trimester. Pelvic ultrasound shows dilated, tortuous pelvic veins consistent with pelvic congestion syndrome. The left-sided predominance of this condition is best explained by which of the following?
choices: Left ovarian vein drains into the higher-pressure left renal vein
Left ovarian vein drains directly into the IVC
Right ovarian vein drains into the inferior mesenteric vein
Right ovarian vein drains into the portal vein
Right ovarian vein drains into the left renal vein
explanations: Correct. The left ovarian vein drains into the left renal vein, which is at higher pressure than the IVC; valvular incompetence at this junction predisposes to reflux and pelvic congestion.
Incorrect. It is the right ovarian vein that drains directly into the IVC.
Incorrect. Ovarian venous drainage is systemic, not portal.
Incorrect. Ovarian venous drainage does not enter the portal system.
Incorrect. The right ovarian vein drains into the IVC, not the left renal vein.

questions.stem: A vascular surgeon is performing a complex pelvic procedure and notes that the umbilical artery gives off vessels that supply the superior aspect of the urinary bladder. The umbilical artery itself is a branch of which of the following vessels?
explanations: Incorrect. The external iliac artery supplies the lower limb, not pelvic viscera.
Incorrect. The inferior epigastric artery is a branch of the external iliac and does not give rise to the umbilical artery.
Incorrect. The inferior mesenteric artery supplies hindgut structures, not the bladder.
Correct. The superior vesical arteries arise from the umbilical artery, which itself is a branch of the internal iliac artery.
Incorrect. The median sacral artery supplies the sacrum and coccyx, not the bladder.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman is undergoing radical nephrectomy for a 6-cm left renal cell carcinoma. As part of staging, the surgeon plans to remove the first-echelon lymph nodes that drain the kidney. Which of the following lymph node groups should be sampled to assess regional metastatic spread?
explanations: Incorrect. Common iliac nodes drain the middle and lower ureter, not the kidney directly.
Incorrect. External iliac nodes receive drainage from the superior bladder and lower limb, not the kidney.
Incorrect. Inguinal nodes drain the lower limb, perineum, and external genitalia.
Incorrect. Internal iliac nodes drain the inferior bladder and pelvic viscera, not the kidney.
Correct. Renal lymph drains primarily into the para-aortic (lumbar) and paracaval nodes; for the left kidney drainage is consistently para-aortic.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man undergoes radical cystectomy for high-grade urothelial carcinoma localized to the dome (superior aspect) of the bladder. The operating urologist plans to sample the first-echelon nodal basin for this tumor location. Which of the following lymph node groups is the primary first-echelon drainage site?
explanations: Incorrect. Common iliac nodes are second-echelon for bladder drainage.
Correct. The superior bladder drains primarily to the external iliac nodes; the inferior bladder drains to the internal iliac nodes.
Incorrect. Internal iliac nodes are first-echelon for the inferior, not superior, bladder.
Incorrect. Para-aortic nodes are the primary drainage for the kidneys.
Incorrect. Superficial inguinal nodes drain perineal skin and external genitalia, not the bladder.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with a complete spinal cord transection at the T8 level retains intact sympathetic outflow that mediates urinary storage. During the storage phase, sympathetic stimulation relaxes the detrusor and contracts the internal urethral sphincter. The sympathetic preganglionic fibers that mediate these effects most likely arise from which of the following spinal cord segments?
questions.diagram:
Autonomic control of micturition
StorageSympathetic L1–L2↓detrusor·↑internal sphincter
VoidingParasympathetic S2–S4↑detrusor·↓internal sphincter
VoluntaryPudendal (somatic, S2–S4)↑/↓external sphincter
explanations: Correct. Sympathetic fibers to the bladder arise from L1–L2 and promote urine storage by relaxing the detrusor and contracting the internal urethral sphincter.
Incorrect. S2–S4 carry parasympathetic fibers that promote voiding, not storage.
Incorrect. S5–Co1 do not provide bladder autonomic innervation.
Incorrect. T6–T8 sympathetic outflow does not innervate the bladder.
Incorrect. T10–L1 sympathetic outflow targets the kidney; bladder sympathetics originate one segment lower.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man develops urinary retention after a cauda equina injury sustained during a motor vehicle collision. He is unable to initiate micturition despite a full bladder. Loss of which of the following fibers most directly explains his inability to contract the detrusor muscle?
choices: Parasympathetic fibers from the vagus nerve
Somatic fibers from the pudendal nerve
explanations: Correct. Parasympathetic fibers from S2–S4 (carried by the pelvic splanchnic nerves) stimulate detrusor contraction; cauda equina injury disrupts these fibers.
Incorrect. Vagal parasympathetic fibers do not innervate the bladder.
Incorrect. The pudendal nerve provides voluntary control of the external urethral sphincter, not detrusor contraction.
Incorrect. Sympathetic fibers from L1–L2 promote bladder relaxation and urine storage.
Incorrect. T10–L1 sympathetics innervate the kidney, not the detrusor.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old G3P3 woman reports involuntary urine leakage when she coughs, laughs, or lifts heavy objects. Her symptoms began 6 months after her third vaginal delivery and have worsened over the past several years. Pelvic exam shows mild anterior vaginal wall prolapse. Urodynamic testing reveals leakage with increases in intra-abdominal pressure and an intact detrusor reflex. Weakness of the muscle innervated by which of the following nerves is most directly responsible for her symptoms?
explanations: Incorrect. The genitofemoral nerve does not innervate the urethral sphincter.
Incorrect. The hypogastric nerve carries sympathetic fibers to the internal urethral sphincter and is not associated with stress incontinence.
Incorrect. The iliohypogastric nerve innervates the lower abdominal wall, not the urethral sphincter.
Incorrect. Pelvic splanchnics carry parasympathetic fibers that promote voiding rather than continence.
Correct. The pudendal nerve provides somatic motor innervation to the external urethral sphincter; weakness manifests as stress incontinence with rises in intra-abdominal pressure.
